fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled URL string from TLV type 1 is set as CURLOPT_URL on the easy handle.
Attacker-controlled u32 value 1 enables redirect following on the easy handle.
Attacker-controlled HTTP 302 response with malicious Location header is stored as the first server response.
Multi perform starts the HTTP transfer; curl connects to the fuzzer socket and receives the 302 response.

fine_trace.code: uc = curl_url_set(data->state.uh, CURLUPART_URL, newurl, (type == FOLLOW_REDIR) ? CURLU_URLENCODE : 0)
fine_trace.note: On receiving the 302 Location header, curl calls curl_url_set with CURLU_URLENCODE to parse the redirect URL, entering the vulnerable seturl path.

fine_trace.code: if((flags & CURLU_URLENCODE) && path[0]) { char *newp = malloc(strlen(path) * 3); ... path = newp; }
fine_trace.note: The redirect path is URL-encoded into a newly allocated buffer newp; path now points to newp and path_alloced is TRUE.
query points into the URL-encoded buffer newp at the '?' separator; the '?' is replaced with NUL, so query now references memory inside newp.

fine_trace.code: char *newp = Curl_dedotdotify(path); ... if(strcmp(newp, path)) { if(path_alloced) free(path); path = newp; }
fine_trace.note: Curl_dedotdotify resolves the ../ sequences and returns a different buffer; free(path) frees the URL-encoded buffer newp, leaving query as a dangling pointer.
strdup(query) reads from the freed newp buffer, causing a heap-use-after-free READ 1.
